correctness.rationale: The polynomial is integral because f squarefree of degree p is not a pth power in k(t); z^p-f is irreducible over k(t). The map onto P1 is finite purely inseparable degree p. Jacobian criterion, F_z=0, and Euler homogeneous identity in characteristic p reduce singularity to vanishing coefficient differential dh on affine charts. At critical point the local value f0 is nonzero (simple roots prevent df=0 at f=0), and its first nonconstant term order m>=2 is <=p-1 because f is degree p, is not a pth power (otherwise multiple root), and derivative degree <=p-2. Since gcd(m,p)=1 an mth-root formal coordinate substitution absorbs the higher unit and yields v^p=u^m; normalization via u=s^p,v=s^m proves semigroup and gap count. Transition of f across P1 charts has degree p, whose derivative cross term vanishes in characteristic p; df is nonzero section O(p-2), so sum critical vanishing multiplicities m-1=p-2 and deltas sum plane arithmetic genus (p-1)(p-2)/2. A unibranch integral curve with zero normalization genus has normalization P1. Independently checked char5 polynomial expansion h(2+u)=3+u²+u^5 and infinity 1+s³+s⁴; semigroup gaps give 2+4=6. These finite checks do not prove all p.
